deterministic rule. At stage $k$ one inspects the
entries in column $k$ from rows $k$ through $n-1$, swaps a row with maximal
entry modulus into row $k$, and then eliminates the entries below that pivot.

$$\rho(A):=\frac{\max_{i,j}|u_{ij}|}{\max_{i,j}|a_{ij}|},$$

provided $A\ne 0$; when $A=0$ one declares $\rho(A)=1$. The absolute value or
modulus is the one from [[def-abs-value]] on real entries and its standard
complex analogue on complex entries.

Let $F$ be a field, let $n\in\mathbb N$ (including $0$), and let $A\in M_{n\times n}(F)$ satisfy
$A_{ij}=A_{ji}$ for every $i,j<n$ (that is, $A$ is symmetric). Its
**structural graph** is
the simple undirected graph $G_0=(V,E_0)$ with vertex set
$V=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and edge set

$$E_0:=\bigl\{\{i,j\}:0\le i<j<n,\ A_{ij}\ne0\bigr\}.$$

An **elimination ordering** is a listing $v_0,\ldots,v_{n-1}$ in which every
vertex of $V$ occurs exactly once. Define the current vertex set by
$V_k=\{v_\ell:k\le\ell<n\}$, starting with the structural graph $G_0$. At
step $k$, the **later neighbors** of $v_k$ are

$$N_k(v_k):=\{u\in V_k\setminus\{v_k\}:\{u,v_k\}\in E_k\}.$$

The filled graph $G_{k+1}=(V_{k+1},E_{k+1})$ is obtained by deleting $v_k$ and
its incident edges, retaining all edges between remaining vertices, and adding
every edge between two distinct vertices of $N_k(v_k)$. An edge added at step
$k$ that was not already in $E_k$ is a **fill edge**. Repeating this rule
defines the symbolic elimination pattern for the ordering; it is defined from
the initial graph and ordering alone, without numerical pivot values.

If $N_k(v_k)$ is nonempty, the **parent** of $v_k$ is the later neighbor
$v_\ell$ with least position $\ell>k$ in the ordering. If $N_k(v_k)$ is
empty, $v_k$ is a root. Each non-root has a unique parent, and positions strictly increase along parent edges, so there is no directed cycle. If the underlying undirected graph had a cycle, its least-position vertex would be a child of both adjacent later vertices, contradicting uniqueness. Thus the parent relation is an elimination forest.

Also replace $Q$ by $E_{kp}Q$, where $E_{kp}$ is the permutation matrix swapping rows $k$ and $p$. Do not change the previously stored rows of $U$. $$S^{(k+1)}_{ij}=S^{(k)}_{ij}-L_{ik}U_{kj}.$$
In a sparse representation it suffices to visit positions where $S^{(k)}_{ij}\ne0$ or $L_{ik}U_{kj}\ne0$; missing entries in this formula are zero. Let $c=S^{(k)}_{ik}$ and $p=S^{(k)}_{kk}$ at a successful pivot. If the diagonal is accepted, [F1] gives $|c/p|\le\theta^{-1}$. If a maximum-modulus entry is selected, $|c/p|\le1\le\theta^{-1}$. The rounded division therefore gives $|\widehat l_{ik}|\le(1+u)/\theta\le2/\theta$. Also every pivot-row entry and every active entry has modulus at most $\rho M$.

For a trailing update, write $p_{ij}=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat l_{ik}\widehat u_{kj})$ and $S^{(k+1)}_{ij}=\operatorname{fl}(S^{(k)}_{ij}-p_{ij})$. Define $e_{ijk}=S^{(k+1)}_{ij}-(S^{(k)}_{ij}-\widehat l_{ik}\widehat u_{kj})$. By [F2]. [given, F1, F2, algebra]
$$|p_{ij}-\widehat l_{ik}\widehat u_{kj}|\le u|\widehat l_{ik}\widehat u_{kj}|, \quad |S^{(k+1)}_{ij}-(S^{(k)}_{ij}-p_{ij})|\le u|S^{(k)}_{ij}-p_{ij}|.$$
The triangle inequality and $|p_{ij}|\le(1+u)|\widehat l_{ik}\widehat u_{kj}|$ yield
$$|e_{ijk}|\le u|S^{(k)}_{ij}|+u(2+u)|\widehat l_{ik}\widehat u_{kj}| \le u\rho M\left(1+\frac{(2+u)(1+u)}{\theta}\right) \le \frac{7u\rho M}{\theta},$$
using $u<1$ and $\theta\le1$.
For a computed multiplier, $\widehat l_{ik}=\operatorname{fl}(c/p)$, so [F2] gives a division residual $e^{\rm div}_{ik}:=c-\widehat l_{ik}p$ with $|e^{\rm div}_{ik}|\le u|c|\le u\rho M$.

Track each active row together with its previously stored entries of $\widehat L$ and its accumulated update residuals. Before stage $k$, for every active row $i$ and active column $j\ge k$, maintain [F1, step 1.2, step 2.1, induction, algebra]
$$
(Q_k P A P^T)_{ij}=\sum_{r<k}\widehat l_{ir}\widehat u_{rj}+S^{(k)}_{ij}-\sum_{r<k}e_{ijr},
$$
where $Q_k$ is the row permutation accumulated so far. At $k=0$ this is $S^{(0)}=PAP^T$. Swapping two active rows also swaps their earlier $L$ entries and residual histories, so it preserves the invariant. After the pivot, $\widehat u_{kj}=S^{(k)}_{kj}$; each lower-row update is $S^{(k+1)}_{ij}=S^{(k)}_{ij}-\widehat l_{ik}\widehat u_{kj}+e_{ijk}$, so substitution gives the same invariant at stage $k+1$. For the pivot column, $S^{(k)}_{ik}=\widehat l_{ik}\widehat u_{kk}+e^{\rm div}_{ik}$ by definition of the division residual. Thus after all stages, for $i\le j$,
$$
(\widehat QPA P^T)_{ij}-(\widehat L\widehat U)_{ij}=-\sum_{k<i}e_{ijk},
$$
and for $i>j$,
$$(\widehat QPA P^T)_{ij}-(\widehat L\widehat U)_{ij} =e^{\rm div}_{ij}-\sum_{k<j}e_{ijk}.$$
These identities define $\Delta A=\widehat L\widehat U-\widehat QPA P^T$. Each entry contains at most $n$ update residuals and at most one division residual.

By steps 1.2–2.1, every residual entry is bounded by [step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]
$$n\frac{7u\rho M}{\theta}+u\rho M \le \frac{8nu}{\theta}\rho M,$$
since $n\ge1$ and $\theta\le1$. Summing at most $n$ such bounds in any row gives $\|\Delta A\|_\infty\le8n^2u\rho M/\theta$.

For $i>j$, the $(i,j)$ entry of $B=RR^*$ is $B_{ij}=\sum_{k<j}r_{ik}\overline{r_{jk}}+r_{ij}\overline{r_{jj}}$. Because $r_{jj}>0$, solving this identity for $r_{ij}$ gives exactly the recurrence in [F1]. Induction on $j$ therefore makes every computed column equal to the corresponding column of $R$.

Let $S^j$ be the exact Schur complement after eliminating positions $0,\ldots,j-1$ from $B$. Initially $S^0=B$. If the first $j$ columns equal those of $R$, then [step 3.1, F1, F2, IH, induction, algebra]

Let $F$ be a field, let $n\in\mathbb N$ (including $0$), and let $A\in M_{n\times n}(F)$ satisfy
$A_{ij}=A_{ji}$ for every $i,j<n$ (that is, $A$ is symmetric). Its
**structural graph** is
the simple undirected graph $G_0=(V,E_0)$ with vertex set
$V=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and edge set

$$E_0:=\bigl\{\{i,j\}:0\le i<j<n,\ A_{ij}\ne0\bigr\}.$$

An **elimination ordering** is a listing $v_0,\ldots,v_{n-1}$ in which every
vertex of $V$ occurs exactly once. Define the current vertex set by
$V_k=\{v_\ell:k\le\ell<n\}$, starting with the structural graph $G_0$. At
step $k$, the **later neighbors** of $v_k$ are

$$N_k(v_k):=\{u\in V_k\setminus\{v_k\}:\{u,v_k\}\in E_k\}.$$

The filled graph $G_{k+1}=(V_{k+1},E_{k+1})$ is obtained by deleting $v_k$ and
its incident edges, retaining all edges between remaining vertices, and adding
every edge between two distinct vertices of $N_k(v_k)$. An edge added at step
$k$ that was not already in $E_k$ is a **fill edge**. Repeating this rule
defines the symbolic elimination pattern for the ordering; it is defined from
the initial graph and ordering alone, without numerical pivot values.

If $N_k(v_k)$ is nonempty, the **parent** of $v_k$ is the later neighbor
$v_\ell$ with least position $\ell>k$ in the ordering. If $N_k(v_k)$ is
empty, $v_k$ is a root. Each non-root has a unique parent, and positions strictly increase along parent edges, so there is no directed cycle. If the underlying undirected graph had a cycle, its least-position vertex would be a child of both adjacent later vertices, contradicting uniqueness. Thus the parent relation is an elimination forest.

Input an integer $k\ge1$ and dimension $d\in\{2,3\}$. The coordinate vertices are $\{0,\ldots,k-1\}^d$. Identify them with the zero-based matrix indices $0,\ldots,k^d-1$ by the lexicographic bijection $q(i_1,\ldots,i_d)=\sum_{a=1}^d i_a k^{d-a}$. The grid graph has an edge between two coordinate vertices exactly when they differ by $1$ in one coordinate and agree in all others. Use the graph and ordering conventions of [[def-symmetric-structural-elimination-graph-and-ordering]] on these indices. Thus $d=2$ gives the five-point graph and $d=3$ the seven-point graph.

Order a rectangular coordinate subbox recursively as follows. For each coordinate whose side length is at least $2$, choose its lower median coordinate, namely the coordinate with $\lfloor(m-1)/2\rfloor$ positions below it in a side of length $m$. Let $S$ be the union of the coordinate hyperplanes at those selected medians. Delete $S$, obtaining at most $2^d$ nonempty rectangular child boxes. Recursively order the child boxes in lexicographic order of their lower corners, then append the vertices of $S$ in lexicographic order. If no coordinate has side length at least $2$, append the remaining vertex as a terminal separator. Apply this rule first to the whole grid. The resulting order is the **coordinate nested-dissection ordering**.

The recursion uses only the graph geometry. It makes no fill or complexity claim for arbitrary graphs.

Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and use the coordinate grid and recursive ordering of [[alg-nested-dissection-ordering-on-regular-grids]]. For a recursion box $B$, let $S_B$ be its median separator; for the terminal one-vertex box take $S_B=B$. Let $\partial^+B$ be the set of grid vertices outside $B$ adjacent to some vertex of $B$. If $v\in S_B$, then every later filled neighbor of $v$ lies in $S_B\cup\partial^+B$. If every side of $B$ has length at most $s$, then
$$
|\{v\}\cup N^+_\pi(v)|\le |S_B|+|\partial^+B|\le 3d\,s^{d-1}.
$$

For distinct remaining vertices $x,y\in V_k$, the pair $\{x,y\}$ is an edge of $G_k$ if and only if the original graph $G_0$ contains a finite walk from $x$ to $y$ all of whose internal vertices belong to $\{v_0,\ldots,v_{k-1}\}$. A walk may repeat vertices; its internal vertices are the entries other than its two endpoints.

Order a rectangular coordinate subbox recursively as follows.
